name: Vals AI: Independent Benchmarks for Legal AI Reasoning
title: Vals AI: Independent Benchmarks for Legal AI Reasoning
answer: Vals AI publishes independent benchmarks and industry reports evaluating legal AI tools and models on realistic legal tasks. Its most useful finding is that AI tools now beat a lawyer control group on document analysis, retrieval and summarisation, but still lose on EDGAR research and redlining, and that reconciling conflicting authority remains the most reliable failure mode across models.

sections.body: Vals AI runs a suite of independent benchmarks and publishes industry reports on legal AI. The material reviewed covers two industry reports, dated 27 February 2025 and 14 October 2025, a legal research benchmark leaderboard with methodology, an AI-detection research blog, and the organisation's homepage. The reports evaluate named commercial legal AI products against a lawyer control group, while the benchmark pages score general and specialist models on legal research tasks. Questions, gold-standard answers and rubrics are authored and peer-reviewed by practising lawyers.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The February 2025 report evaluated four legal AI tools across seven tasks: data extraction, document Q&A, document summarisation, redlining, transcript analysis, chronology generation and EDGAR research. Harvey Assistant took top scores on five tasks and beat the lawyer baseline on four. CoCounsel scored between 73.2% and 89.6% across its four tasks and topped document summarisation. The AI tools collectively beat the lawyer baseline on document analysis, retrieval and extraction, matched it on chronology generation, and lost on EDGAR research and redlining. The October 2025 report tested Alexi, Counsel Stack, Midpage and ChatGPT on 200 US legal research questions, weighted 50% accuracy, 40% authoritativeness and 10% appropriateness. All AI products scored 74% to 78%, within nine points of the lawyer baseline at 69%, and all beat it on every criterion. Counsel Stack scored highest. The legal research benchmark found a three-way tie at the top on 55.29% all-pass accuracy, with health and administrative or regulatory questions scoring highest and family and immigration hardest.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Harvey Assistant scored 94.8% on document Q&A and 80.2% on chronology generation, matching the lawyer baseline. CoCounsel averaged 79.5% across four tasks and beat the lawyer baseline there by more than ten points. Document Q&A averaged 80.2% overall, the highest-scoring task. In the research study, accuracy ran 78% to 81% for legal AI products and 80% for the generalist product. On the legal research benchmark, reconciling conflicting authority cost every model six to seventeen points, eleven points pooled. Mean all-pass accuracy ranged from 43.9% in health down to 13.7% in family.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: This source gives a reader following AI in legal a vendor-neutral view of what legal AI actually does well and where it fails. The task-level results show document analysis, retrieval and summarisation are largely solved relative to a lawyer baseline, while EDGAR research and redlining remain weak. The research benchmark isolates a specific failure mode, synthesising across jurisdictions, courts or regimes, which is more useful than a single headline score. The cost and latency data let a reader weigh accuracy against price per task when choosing a model.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Legal

sections.body: The reports cover a small number of named commercial products and a lawyer control group, not a full market. Lexis+AI withdrew from the sections studied, and Harvey opted into six of seven tasks, so coverage is uneven. The benchmark pages mix legal and non-legal evaluations, and the homepage is largely navigation and leaderboard listings. The AI-detection research concerns writing samples rather than legal work, and its authors state they are unsure how results generalise outside their specific distribution.
